newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher on Tuesday, with economic data continuing to support the bond market.
U.S. November Consumer Confidence remained at a strong 107.3, was said to be in line with expectations, and added a little positive sentiment to Dutch bonds, dealers said.
Trade was concentrated on the short end and on corporate paper, although a lack of sellers pushed up 2023 bonds. There was also some switching along the curve, dealers said.
"Players try to increase their performance without increasing the risk," one dealer said.
Dealers said, as well as switching along the curve, there were some plays between Dutch bonds and German bunds, but there was no clear direction to these trades.
The 10-year spread with German bunds widened during the day, closing at -6 basis points vs -4 basis points on Monday, but dealers said the spread could easily tighten further or even disappear.
"If there is a real rally, Germany always wins," said one dealer.
Others said that, although fundamentally the Dutch yield should be above Germany's, this was unlikely to happen soon.
"That is an old story, but it never actually works out," one dealer said.
